content.title: JPMorgan stock tumbles over 4% after company warns on higher spending in 2026
content.summary: JPMorgan stock was the biggest loser in the Dow on Tuesday following comments from a top executive on higher costs for the firm in 2026.

content.title: JPMorgan Stock Drops After Bank Predicts $105 Billion in Expenses Next Year
content.summary: JPMorgan Chase’s stock fell more than 4.7% on Tuesday after the bank told investors that it will spend billions of dollars more in expenses next year.  At the Goldman Sachs conference in New York on Tuesday, consumer chief Marianne Lake told investors that the bank had just completed budgeting for next year and is planning to spend $105 billion, largely because of higher costs in her division.  The bank is expecting expenses this year to be $95.9 billion and analysts had anticipated approximately $101 billion of expenses next year, according to FactSet.

content.title: JPMorgan’s Stock Slide Weighs on Dow Industrials
content.summary: The blue-chip index fell 0.4%, dragged down by JPMorgan Chase shares, ahead of the Fed’s rate decision. The S&P 500 slipped 0.1%, while the Nasdaq added 0.1%.

content.title: Top Analyst Reports for JPMorgan Chase, EPAM & Costco
content.summary: New analyst reports spotlight JPMorgan Chase as operational strength, NII prospects and cost pressures shape its outlook.

content.title: JPMorgan Stock Sinks on Higher Expense Outlook. Other Banks May Have to Keep Up.
content.summary: The nation’s largest bank said new growth initiatives, plus inflation, would driving expenses higher in 2026.

content.title: JPMorgan shares drop as bank warns of fragile consumers, higher costs
content.summary: Investing.com -- JPMorgan Chase (NYSE:JPM) stock fell 4.3% by 2 pm Tuesday after the bank’s consumer and community banking CEO Marianne Lake warned of a "bit more fragile" consumer environment and projected higher-than-expected expenses for 2026.

content.title: JPMorgan Hires Vaunted Berkshire Stockpicker as Buffett’s Exit Spurs C-Suite Shakeup
content.summary: On Monday Berkshire also announced that CFO Marc Hamburg, who has held the role for 40 years, plans to retire in June.

content.title: Combs’ Departure from Berkshire Leaves a Gap in Managing Equity Portfolio
content.summary: The coming departure of Berkshire manager Todd Combs to  JPMorgan Chase  leaves questions about who will manage  Berkshire Hathaway’s  $300 billion equity portfolio when CEO Warren Buffett retires at the end of 2025.  Combs move to JPMorgan is a loss for Berkshire given his dual role as an investment manager and CEO of Geico, Berkshire’s auto insurance unit.

content.title: Berkshire’s Geico Boss Todd Combs Leaves for JPMorgan Ahead of Buffett Retirement
content.summary: A top lieutenant is departing for a role at JPMorgan Chase as Greg Abel takes over as CEO, and CFO Marc Hamburg will step down from his role in June.
